sector_model: nonfinancial consumer internet and dealer software marketplace; use GAAP earnings, FCF after capitalized website costs, SBC and cash tax normalization, net cash
thesis: CarGurus runs the most visited U.S. car shopping site and sells listings and software to about 34.7K dealers. After a 6.7% fall to 33.74 on 2026-11-06 (the day after Q3 results) it trades near 16.0x TTM GAAP earnings from continuing operations and a 10.0% TTM FCF yield (after capitalized website costs), with no financial debt and 164.9M cash. Q3 revenue grew 12% with 92% gross margin, guidance for 2026 revenue is 1,011.5 to 1,016.5M (+11.5% to 12.1%), and the share count is down 8.2% year on year through buybacks (225M in 9M26).
counterthesis: Growth is price (consolidated QARSD +7%) more than volume (paying dealers +3%), so the dealer base is only slowly expanding; consumer traffic is exposed to AI search and Google changes and to the used car cycle. 9M26 GAAP net income from continuing ops fell 6% as sales and marketing (+16%) and a 20.2M impairment outran revenue. The 10.0% FCF yield is flattered: cash taxes paid were only 7.1M versus a 39.0M provision (deferred tax asset use, DTA still 68.2M), stock compensation is about 51.5M TTM (15% of FCF), and TTM operating cash flow includes unseparated discontinued CarOffer cash flows for 2025. Buybacks exceed free cash flow so cash fell and the 2026 authorization has only 25M left (a new 250M program was announced 2026-11-05 per release). Failed CarOffer wind-down shows capital allocation misses. Operating lease liabilities of 182.3M are debt like. Cause of the 6.7% drop on 11-06 not identified.
invalidation: Paying dealer count falling for two quarters or QARSD growth under 3%; revenue growth below 8%; operating margin falling because sales and marketing keep growing faster than revenue; FCF falling below GAAP earnings once tax normalizes; buybacks funded by drawing the revolver; evidence of material consumer traffic loss to AI assistants.
